title: Szemerédi Regularity vs. Frieze-Kannan Weak Regularity
description: Formalizes the Frieze-Kannan (FK) weak regularity lemma and proves that every ε-regular partition (Szemerédi) is a 2ε-cut-approximation (Frieze-Kannan). Establishes the strict hierarchy: Szemerédi regularity implies FK weak regularity, but not vice versa. Compares the tower-type bound of Szemerédi against FK's single exponential 4^(1/ε²).

meta.author: Frieze, Kannan (1999); Szemerédi (1978)

overview.historicalContext:
Szemerédi's Regularity Lemma (1978) is one of the most powerful tools in extremal combinatorics. Originally developed as a lemma to prove Szemerédi's theorem on arithmetic progressions (1975 — itself resolving a 1936 Erdős-Turán conjecture), the lemma states that every sufficiently large graph can be partitioned into a bounded number of vertex classes such that most pairs of classes are 'ε-regular' — the edge density between large subsets closely approximates the density between the entire classes. The price is severe: the number of parts may be as large as a tower function tower(1/ε) — a stack of exponentials of height proportional to 1/ε. In 1997, Gowers proved this tower bound is necessary: no partition into only singly exponentially many parts can guarantee ε-regularity for all graphs.

Frieze and Kannan (1999) introduced a weaker 'cut regularity' condition motivated by matrix approximation problems in theoretical computer science. Their version asks only that a partition approximates the graph's edge density globally — the total cut error over ALL pairs (A,B) ⊆ V is ≤ ε·n², rather than requiring per-pair regularity. This global guarantee requires at most 4^(1/ε²) parts — singly exponential, not tower. Frieze-Kannan (FK) regularity is strictly weaker: there exist graphs where every ε-cut-approximation has pairs that are not ε-regular. The FK version has superior computational properties: FK-regular partitions can be found in polynomial time O(n^{2+1/ε²}) using randomized algorithms, while Szemerédi regularity requires exponential time in the worst case (Alon, Duke, Lefmann, Rödl, Yuster, 2007).

The relationship between the two notions forms a strict hierarchy — Szemerédi regularity implies FK cut-approximation, but not conversely — making FK an attractive alternative for applications where the global cut guarantee suffices. Key applications of FK regularity include the regularity-based graph algorithms of Frieze-Kannan (sampling graph properties, counting structures), the property testing framework of Alon-Fischer-Krivelevich-Szegedy, and the foundations of graphon theory (Lovász-Szegedy, 2007), which abstracts regularity to the analytic setting of bounded symmetric measurable functions on [0,1]².

This file proves the Szemerédi ⟹ FK implication formally in Lean 4, using Mathlib's existing SzemerediRegularity library as the foundation, and quantifies the tower-vs-singly-exponential gap with explicit Lean computations.
overview.problemStatement: Prove that every ε-regular partition in the sense of Szemerédi is a 2ε-cut-approximation in the sense of Frieze-Kannan. Establish the quantitative comparison: Szemerédi requires ≤ tower(1/ε) parts while FK requires ≤ 4^(1/ε²) parts.
overview.text: Formalizes the Frieze-Kannan weak regularity lemma and its relationship to Szemerédi regularity. The central theorem: any ε-regular partition (Szemerédi's condition) satisfies the FK cut-approximation property with parameter 2ε. The converse fails — a cut-approximation need not be ε-regular. Quantitative bound comparison is also proved.
overview.proofStrategy: The main theorem `szemeredi_implies_fk` follows from `pair_cut_error_bound`: for each pair (Pᵢ, Pⱼ) of parts in an ε-regular partition, the cut error is ≤ 2ε|Pᵢ||Pⱼ|. Summing over all pairs and using the partition identity Σᵢⱼ|Pᵢ||Pⱼ| = n² gives global cut error ≤ 2ε·n². The per-pair bound handles two cases: (1) when A,B are 'large' (≥ ε fraction of their parts), ε-regularity gives |d(A,B)-d(P,Q)| ≤ ε, and (2) when A or B is 'small', the trivial bound |e| ≤ |A||B| gives the needed estimate.
keyInsights: The Frieze-Kannan condition is a global cut-norm approximation: ‖W_G - W_P‖_□ ≤ ε, where the cut norm is taken over ALL pairs A,B not just within-partition subsets
The per-pair lemma needs two cases: 'large' A,B (where ε-regularity applies directly) and 'small' A,B (where the trivial bound |e| ≤ |A||B| ≤ ε|P||Q| gives 2ε|P||Q|)
The crucial partition identity Σᵢⱼ|Pᵢ||Pⱼ| = n² allows converting per-pair bounds to a global bound on the cut approximation quality
Szemerédi's stepBound n = n·4^n grows tower-type over iterations, while FK's 4^(1/ε²) bound is singly exponential — this quantitative gap is explicit in the formalization
The converse (FK ⟹ Szemerédi) fails: a cut-approximation partition need not be ε-regular; the FK condition is strictly weaker

The factor-of-2 in the main theorem (ε-regular ⟹ 2ε-cut-approx) is sharp: it arises from bounding both e(A,B) and d|A||B| each by ε|P||Q| in the small-set case, and cannot be reduced to 1 with this proof strategy

FK regularity is algorithmically favorable: Frieze-Kannan (1999) showed it can be computed in polynomial time O(n^{2+1/ε²}), whereas Szemerédi regularity requires exponential time in the worst case (Alon et al. 2007); for graph approximation and property testing, FK often suffices

**Graphon theory: FK as finite-graph cut-metric approximation**: The FK cut-approximation condition is precisely the discrete version of approximation in the cut metric on graphons. A graphon is a bounded symmetric measurable function $W: [0,1]^2 \to [0,1]$; its cut norm is $\|W\|_\square = \sup_{S,T \subseteq [0,1]} |\int_{S\times T} W|$. The FK condition $\|W_G - W_P\|_\square \leq \varepsilon$ (where $W_G$ is the graphon of $G$ and $W_P$ the step-function graphon of partition $P$) is exactly what this file formalizes (in the finite-graph language as $|e(A,B) - \text{predicted}| \leq \varepsilon n^2$). The Lovász-Szegedy (2007) compactness theorem for graphons — every sequence of dense graphs has a convergent subsequence in cut metric — is the analytic analog of the FK regularity lemma's existence guarantee. The Szemerédi ⟹ FK implication proved here is the finite-graph avatar of the graphon compactness fact: if a graph satisfies the strong (Szemerédi) condition, it automatically satisfies the weak (FK/cut-metric) condition, just as convergence of Szemerédi-type partitions implies convergence in cut metric.

**The cut norm is NP-hard to compute exactly, but FK gives a PTAS**: Computing the cut norm $\|W_G\|_\square = \max_{A,B \subseteq V} |e(A,B)|/n^2$ exactly is equivalent to MAX-CUT, which is NP-hard. The FK regularity partition sidesteps this: on a FK-regular partition $P$ with $k$ parts, the cut norm is approximated by $\max_{i,j} d(P_i,P_j) \pm \varepsilon$, which requires only $k^2 = O(4^{2/\varepsilon^2})$ comparisons. Frieze and Kannan (1999) used this to design polynomial-time approximation schemes for MAX-CUT and MAX-BISECTION on dense graphs (constant average degree $\Omega(n)$): find an FK partition, evaluate the optimization over partition classes, and the error is bounded by the cut-approximation quality $2\varepsilon n^2$. This application justifies the entire FK regularity framework as a bridge from NP-hard combinatorial optimization to polynomial-time approximation.
prerequisites: Szemerédi regularity lemma and ε-regular pairs (SzemerediRegularity.lean)

sections.title: Module Header and Imports
sections.summary: Module documentation comparing Szemerédi and FK regularity with a comparison table. Imports `Mathlib`, `Proofs.SzemerediCore` (ε-regularity infrastructure), and `Proofs.SzemerediRegularity` (parent lemma). Opens `Szemeredi.Core`, `Szemeredi.Regularity`, `Classical`. Declares universe-polymorphic `variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]`.
sections.mathContext: The three imports form the dependency chain: `SzemerediCore` provides `IsEpsilonRegular`, `edgeDensity : ℚ`, and the ε-regularity predicate; `SzemerediRegularity` provides `Finpartition.IsEquipartition` and the full regularity lemma; `Mathlib` supplies `Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs`, `Finset.sum_product`, and rational arithmetic. The `Classical` open enables non-constructive reasoning (decidability instances).

sections.title: Part I: FK Cut Approximation Definition
sections.summary: Defines `IsCutApproximation`: a partition `parts` of V is an ε-cut-approximation of G if for every A, B ⊆ V, the edge count e(A,B) differs from the predicted count Σᵢⱼ d(Pᵢ,Pⱼ)|A∩Pᵢ||B∩Pⱼ| by at most ε·n².
sections.mathContext: Cut approximation: $|e(A,B) - \sum_{ij} d(P_i,P_j)|A\cap P_i||B\cap P_j|| \leq \varepsilon n^2$

sections.title: Part II: Per-Pair Cut Error Bound
sections.summary: Proves `pair_cut_error_bound`: for an ε-regular pair (P,Q) and any A⊆P, B⊆Q, the cut error is |e(A,B) - d(P,Q)|A||B|| ≤ 2ε|P||Q|. The proof splits into large (ε-regularity applies) and small (trivial bound) subcases.

sections.title: Part III: Partition Sum Identities
sections.summary: Proves `edge_count_partition_sum` (e(A,B) = Σᵢⱼ e(A∩Pᵢ,B∩Pⱼ)) and `parts_product_sum_eq_card_sq` (Σᵢⱼ|Pᵢ||Pⱼ| = n²). These identities are essential for converting per-pair bounds to global cut-approximation.
sections.mathContext: $\sum_{ij}|P_i||P_j| = n^2$ — partition product identity enabling global bound

sections.title: Part IV: Szemerédi Implies Frieze-Kannan
sections.summary: Proves `szemeredi_implies_fk`: every ε-regular partition is a 2ε-cut-approximation. Combines the per-pair bound and partition identities. The constant 2 is sharp: regularity gives ε per-pair, and summing two contributions yields 2ε globally.

sections.title: Part V: Bound Comparison (Tower vs. Singly Exponential)
sections.summary: Quantifies the gap between Szemerédi and FK: `sz_stepBound_ge_power` shows stepBound n ≥ 4^n, `sz_two_steps_tower` shows the 2-step bound ≥ 4^(4^n), and `fk_bound_at_half` gives FK bound 4^4 = 256 at ε = 1/2.
sections.mathContext: FK: $\leq 4^{1/\varepsilon^2}$ parts. Szemerédi: $\geq 4^{4^n}$ after 2 steps. Exponential gap confirmed.

conclusion.summary: Proves the strict hierarchy between Szemerédi regularity and Frieze-Kannan cut-approximation: ε-regular ⟹ 2ε-cut-approx. The converse fails. Szemerédi's bound is tower-type (4^(4^n) in 2 steps) while FK's bound is singly exponential (4^(1/ε²)). All results are fully formalized with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications:
The FK weak regularity condition is algorithmically favorable: it can be computed in polynomial time (Frieze-Kannan 1999), while Szemerédi's regularity requires exponential time in the worst case. The formalization establishes the theoretical foundation for studying when the simpler FK guarantee suffices for combinatorial applications (counting lemmas, graph removal, property testing).

The strict hierarchy Szemerédi ⟹ FK (but not conversely) has practical significance: many graph approximation problems that were thought to require the full Szemerédi regularity lemma can be solved using FK regularity alone, with exponentially fewer partition classes. Frieze and Kannan used FK regularity to design polynomial-time algorithms for approximating MAX-CUT, MAX-BISECTION, and related constraint satisfaction problems on dense graphs.

The connection to graphon theory is deep: the FK condition is exactly the discrete version of cut-metric convergence in the space of graphons. Lovász's graph limit theory (developed in a series of papers 2006–2012 with Szegedy, Borgs, Chayes, and others) shows that a sequence of dense graphs converges in the cut metric if and only if the corresponding step-function graphons converge in the cut distance. FK regularity is thus the finite-graph analog of graphon approximation, making this formalization a stepping stone toward a formal treatment of graph limit theory in Lean 4.
openQuestions: Can the converse direction (FK cut-approx ⟹ Szemerédi regularity) be formalized with an explicit counterexample? Random bipartite graphs provide a probabilistic witness: with high probability, a random graph G(n, 1/2) has an FK-regular partition into k classes for small k, yet any ε-regular partition requires tower(1/ε) parts. Can a constructive counterexample be formalized in Lean?

Can the factor-of-2 constant in `szemeredi_implies_fk` be improved to 1, or is 2 tight? The current bound uses |e| ≤ ε|P||Q| and d|A||B| ≤ ε|P||Q| separately in the small-set case. A different proof strategy (treating the two contributions jointly) might achieve a tighter constant.

Can the polynomial-time FK regularity algorithm be formalized in Lean 4? Frieze-Kannan (1999) give a randomized algorithm using random sampling: choose s = O(1/ε²) random vertices, form a partition based on edge densities to these vertices, and output it as an FK-regular partition. The algorithm runs in O(n^{2+1/ε²}) time. Formalizing it would require randomized algorithm theory in Lean.

Gowers (1997) proved the tower-type bound for Szemerédi regularity is necessary. Can this lower bound be formalized? The construction uses quasi-random graphs: sequences of graphs with specific spectral properties that force any ε-regular partition to have tower-many parts. This would complement the upper bound already in Mathlib.

Can the graphon interpretation of FK regularity be formalized? The FK condition ‖W_G - W_P‖_□ ≤ ε (where W_G is the graphon of G and W_P is the step-function graphon of the partition) requires defining the cut metric on the space of graphons, a bounded symmetric measurable function on [0,1]². The Lovász-Szegedy (2007) paper develops this theory; formalizing it would connect the discrete FK regularity to the analytic graphon limit theory.

The counting lemma (Komlós-Simonovits) says that if a graph has an ε-regular partition, then the number of copies of any fixed graph H is approximately what you'd expect from the densities. Can a version for FK regularity be proved and formalized? FK regularity implies a weaker counting lemma with larger error terms — making the FK-vs-Szemerédi tradeoff quantitatively precise for counting applications.

crossReferences.description: Parent: the Szemerédi Regularity Lemma formalization. This file compares Szemerédi regularity with the weaker FK cut-approximation, proving the hierarchy Szemerédi ⟹ FK with explicit partition bounds.

Provides the core definitions used throughout: `IsEpsilonRegular`, `edgeDensity : ℚ`, and the ε-regularity predicate for pairs. This file imports `Proofs.SzemerediCore` directly — it is the algebraic foundation on which both Szemerédi and FK regularity are built.

Szemerédi's theorem on arithmetic progressions (1975) was the original motivation for the regularity lemma. Any sufficiently long subset of the integers contains k-term arithmetic progressions — proved using an early form of the regularity lemma. The FK regularity lemma studied here arose from later work on algorithmic aspects of graph regularity applied to dense structures.

The full Szemerédi regularity formalization in Lean 4. This file builds on it, adding the FK comparison. Together they demonstrate the complete regularity hierarchy: the core lemma (SzemerediCore), the full regularity theorem (SzemerediRegularity), and the FK comparison (this entry).

The hypergraph regularity lemma — a version of Szemerédi regularity for k-uniform hypergraphs. Hypergraph regularity has even larger bounds than graph regularity (iterated tower functions), making the FK comparison even more dramatic in the hypergraph setting. This file's methodology (global cut-approximation) extends to hypergraphs via the 'weak' hypergraph regularity of Chung and Frankl-Rödl.

The Szemerédi counting lemma: given an ε-regular partition, the number of copies of any fixed graph H is approximately what a random graph with the same densities would have. FK regularity implies a weaker counting lemma — the FK ⟹ Szemerédi gap translates into a gap in the counting lemma's error terms, making the Szemerédi-vs-FK distinction quantitatively concrete.

Ramsey's theorem guarantees the existence of monochromatic complete subgraphs in any 2-coloring of a complete graph. Szemerédi regularity provides a structural alternative: instead of complete subgraphs, it guarantees quasi-random structure in almost all pairs. The regularity lemma is now a standard tool for proving Ramsey-type results in dense graphs — FK regularity provides the same structural guarantee with a better partition bound.

Erdős problem #1036 concerns arithmetic progressions and density conditions — closely related to Szemerédi's theorem. The Szemerédi Regularity Lemma was originally developed to prove Szemerédi's theorem on arithmetic progressions in dense subsets of integers; the FK lemma arose from algorithmic work building on those ideas. Both lemmas serve as tools for counting arithmetic progressions in dense sets.

Erdős problem #417 on graph ramsey multiplicity. The Szemerédi regularity machinery — including FK regularity — is a standard tool for analyzing graph density and subgraph counts in dense graphs, precisely the setting of graph Ramsey multiplicity problems.

Hypergraph regularity sub-entry proving bounds for k-uniform hypergraphs. The FK vs. Szemerédi gap is even more extreme for hypergraphs: the hypergraph Szemerédi regularity lemma requires iterated tower bounds (tower of towers), while the Chung-Frankl-Rödl weak hypergraph regularity analog of FK gives only singly or doubly exponential bounds. This entry's methodology (global cut-approximation is weaker than per-part regularity) extends naturally to the hypergraph setting.
